critic12.actualMiswording: tests/jest.setup.ts:97-98 says restoreAllMocks may remove the global mock and warns against using it. Installed Jest runtime delegates restoration to jest-mock, which restores registered spies AND jest.replaceProperty restorers; it does not clear module factories. The older review's 'spies only' proposal is also incomplete.
critic12.factoryVsMapper: Setup's explicit jest.mock('better-sqlite3', factory) supplies an ES-module-shaped default jest.fn returning mockDbMethods. Jest consults the explicit factory registry before loading a mock module. The exact moduleNameMapper separately resolves the package root to tests/__mocks__/better-sqlite3.cjs, whose exports are an object, not that constructor factory. They are distinct mechanisms/shapes. jest.requireActual on the package root bypasses the factory but still resolves through the mapper; existing subpath/absolute-path real-driver bypasses avoid the exact root mapper.
narrowIndependentBehaviourProofBeforeAny: Small Node and jsdom controls using existing setup: matcher registration succeeds; default constructor factory and @/lib/db mock methods retain identity and implementations after restoreAllMocks.
Create one spy and one replaceProperty control; restoreAllMocks restores their originals while an ordinary jest.fn and explicit module-factory export remain intact.

Compare ordinary root import/requireMock with requireActual('better-sqlite3'): prove factory constructor versus mapped CJS object semantics, including the exact resolved path. Preserve fs-mocked safety.
Prove the established subpath/absolute-path bypass still opens and closes a disposable in-memory real SQLite database, without altering the mapper or native-driver fixtures.
